I went mushroom foraging today with some coworkers, and we found Chanterelles. Finally!

I tried last week but came away empty handed aside for some Dewberries and wild fennel.

Today, in Mississippi, near the border with Louisiana, about an hour outside of New Orleans, was where we "found" the bounty. The property is owned by a coworker's family and there were so many mushrooms that in some areas I couldn't take a step without crushing one. I estimate that we gathered about 30 lbs. If we had stayed longer we could have gathered 3x more. It was hard to leave when the forest floor was scattered with golden mushrooms everywhere we looked.

Since I expressed me desire to go and my interest in mycology, they graciously took me along, and while I was there I also took some Oak suckers, that had thankfully already rooted, from the oak trees responsible for the chanterelles (Chanterelles are mycorrhizal and therefore, require a symbiotic relationship with a tree), as well as soil and mycelium from where the mushrooms were popping up. I plan on replanting these saplings (which are probably already inoculated with the fungus) in the soil I collected, and then replanting them on my own property in about 18 months. Hopefully, I can successfully cultivate chanterelles. I also took a few spores prints and will try a separate technique, attempting to inoculate already mature trees with the spores.

I guess I'll let everyone know in 3-5 years if my attempts at culivation were successful, but in the mean time, we still picked a bunch of delicious mushrooms!!

Chanterelles have faux gills, and don't release many spores. They are golden/yellow/orange, with white flesh. Chanterelle lookalikes will have real gills, yellow flesh (inside as well as out), and look "wetter."

After taking some spore prints I cooked mine in butter, diced onion and garlic, and served it with braised short ribs and cauliflower. They're delicious. Anyone who says they hate mushrooms have never tried these!!
And finally, Chanterelles! A successful mushroom foraging trip.

I have been meaning to create a subverse like this for some time. Just my own personal subverse, but open for anyone else to share what they enjoy as well. I will use this sub to post anything I enjoy be it a poem, video, picture, thought, wisdom, etc. This is just for fun. My rules are two-fold;

1) Be respectful. I don't expect you to agree with everyone on everything - it would make the world a boring place. But please, if you cannot find kindness in your heart, at least show respect. We're all human, we're all trying to figure this life out. Don't belittle others just because they see the world a bit different.

2) If there is a disagreement, please choose to resolve it with critical thinking - like the Socratic method. If you are butting heads with another, and do not feel like stepping away from your keyboard, please *try* to see the situation from an outsider's perspective. Often we hold on to what be believe to be truths simply because we have them embedded in our minds. We are prideful creatures that do not like to be wrong. If you cannot find common ground or new perspective, I highly suggest you end the debate.

When I came here last year I was reading a lot on Buddhism. I am not a Buddhist, but I do respect and follow a lot of Siddhartha's philosophies. This lead me to the middle way or middle path, which is obviously an influence on my username. For too long I have felt almost a disconnect from people since they tend to lean very hard on certain issues. I am fine with convictions - I have them myself, but I can't understand complete unwavering ignorance. I cannot, for example, decide if God exists. It's not really something I have seen conclusive reasoning or evidence in either direction, so I remain agnostic until I am convinced. Some call this fence sitting, but I call it critical (albeit irrelevant) thought. I suppose I am going off on a tangent.

v/ThePath is not simply just a dump for things I enjoy, it can hopefully be a path of enlightenment for others. I don't claim to know what that is or how to get there, but I do feel much more spiritual these days. Either way, if you're new or reading this - hello! And welcome to the path!
